verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.68
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 7.68

verses.pali: 7. Mahāvagga
verses.english: 7. The Great Chapter

verses.pali: Dhammaññūsutta
verses.english: One Who Knows the Teachings

verses.pali: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
verses.english: “A mendicant with seven qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

verses.pali: Katamehi sattahi?
verses.english: What seven?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaññū ca hoti atthaññū ca attaññū ca mattaññū ca kālaññū ca parisaññū ca puggalaparoparaññū ca.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, has self-knowledge, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals high and low.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaññū hoti?
verses.english: And how is a mendicant one who knows the teachings?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ jānāti—
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows the teachings:

verses.pali: suttaṁ geyyaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ gāthaṁ udānaṁ itivuttakaṁ jātakaṁ abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ.
verses.english: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ jāneyya—
verses.english: If a mendicant did not know these teachings,

verses.pali: suttaṁ geyyaṁ …pe… abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ, nayidha ‘dhammaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: they would not be called ‘one who knows the teachings’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ jānāti—
verses.english: But because they do know these teachings,

verses.pali: suttaṁ geyyaṁ …pe… abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ, tasmā ‘dhammaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: they are called ‘one who knows the teachings’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings.

verses.pali: Atthaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who knows the meaning?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tassa tasseva bhāsitassa atthaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows the meaning of this or that statement:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho, ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho’ti.
verses.english: ‘This is what that statement means; that is what this statement means.’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tassa tasseva bhāsitassa atthaṁ jāneyya:
verses.english: If a mendicant did not know the meaning of this or that statement,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho, ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho’ti, nayidha ‘atthaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: they would not be called ‘one who knows the meaning’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tassa tasseva bhāsitassa atthaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But because they do know the meaning of this or that statement,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho, ayaṁ imassa bhāsitassa attho’ti, tasmā ‘atthaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: they are called ‘one who knows the meaning’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū, atthaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings and the one who knows the meaning.

verses.pali: Attaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who has self-knowledge?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attānaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant has self-knowledge:

verses.pali: ‘ettakomhi saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānenā’ti.
verses.english: ‘This is the extent of my faith, ethics, learning, generosity, wisdom, and eloquence.’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attānaṁ jāneyya:
verses.english: If a mendicant did not have self-knowledge,

verses.pali: ‘ettakomhi saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānenā’ti, nayidha ‘attaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: they would not be called ‘one who has self-knowledge’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attānaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But because they do have self-knowledge,

verses.pali: ‘ettakomhi saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānenā’ti, tasmā ‘attaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: they are called ‘one who has self-knowledge’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū, atthaññū, attaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings, the one who knows the meaning, and the one who has self-knowledge.

verses.pali: Mattaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who knows moderation?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mattaṁ jānāti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ paṭiggahaṇāya.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows moderation when receiving robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mattaṁ jāneyya cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ paṭiggahaṇāya, nayidha ‘mattaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: If a mendicant did not know moderation, they would not be called ‘one who knows moderation’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mattaṁ jānāti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ paṭiggahaṇāya, tasmā ‘mattaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: But because they do know moderation, they are called ‘one who knows moderation’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū, atthaññū, attaññū, mattaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings, the one who knows the meaning, the one who has self-knowledge, and the one who knows moderation.

verses.pali: Kālaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who knows the right time?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows the right time:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ kālo uddesassa, ayaṁ kālo paripucchāya, ayaṁ kālo yogassa, ayaṁ kālo paṭisallānassā’ti.
verses.english: ‘This is the time for recitation; this is the time for questioning; this is the time for meditation; this is the time for retreat.’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālaṁ jāneyya:
verses.english: If a mendicant did not know the right time,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ kālo uddesassa, ayaṁ kālo paripucchāya, ayaṁ kālo yogassa, ayaṁ kālo paṭisallānassā’ti, nayidha ‘kālaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: they would not be called ‘one who knows the right time’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But because they do know the right time,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ kālo uddesassa, ayaṁ kālo paripucchāya, ayaṁ kālo yogassa, ayaṁ kālo paṭisallānassā’ti, tasmā ‘kālaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: they are called ‘one who knows the right time’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū, atthaññū, attaññū, mattaññū, kālaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings, the one who knows the meaning, the one who has self-knowledge, the one who knows moderation, and the one who knows the right time.

verses.pali: Parisaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who knows assemblies?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows assemblies:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ khattiyaparisā, ayaṁ brāhmaṇaparisā, ayaṁ gahapatiparisā, ayaṁ samaṇaparisā.
verses.english: ‘This is an assembly of aristocrats, of brahmins, of householders, or of ascetics.

verses.pali: Tattha evaṁ upasaṅkamitabbaṁ, evaṁ ṭhātabbaṁ, evaṁ kattabbaṁ, evaṁ nisīditabbaṁ, evaṁ bhāsitabbaṁ, evaṁ tuṇhī bhavitabban’ti.
verses.english: This one should be approached in this way. This is how to stand, to act, to sit, to speak, or to stay silent when there.’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisaṁ jāneyya:
verses.english: If a mendicant did not know assemblies,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ khattiyaparisā …pe…
evaṁ tuṇhī bhavitabban’ti, nayidha ‘parisaññū’ti vucceyya.
verses.english: they would not be called ‘one who knows assemblies’.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But because they do know assemblies,

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ khattiyaparisā, ayaṁ brāhmaṇaparisā, ayaṁ gahapatiparisā, ayaṁ samaṇaparisā.
Tattha evaṁ upasaṅkamitabbaṁ, evaṁ ṭhātabbaṁ, evaṁ kattabbaṁ, evaṁ nisīditabbaṁ, evaṁ bhāsitabbaṁ, evaṁ tuṇhī bhavitabban’ti, tasmā ‘parisaññū’ti vuccati.
verses.english: they are called ‘one who knows assemblies’.

verses.pali: Iti dhammaññū, atthaññū, attaññū, mattaññū, kālaññū, parisaññū.
verses.english: Such is the one who knows the teachings, the one who knows the meaning, the one who has self-knowledge, the one who knows moderation, the one who knows the right time, and the one who knows assemblies.

verses.pali: Puggalaparoparaññū ca kathaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how are they one who knows individuals high and low?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dvayena puggalā viditā honti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant understands individuals in terms of pairs.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā—
verses.english: Two individuals:

verses.pali: eko ariyānaṁ dassanakāmo, eko ariyānaṁ na dassanakāmo.
verses.english: one likes to see the noble ones, one does not.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo ariyānaṁ na dassanakāmo,
verses.english: The individual who doesn’t like to see the noble ones

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo ariyānaṁ dassanakāmo,
verses.english: The individual who does like to see the noble ones

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .1
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā ariyānaṁ dassanakāmā—
verses.english: Two individuals like to see the noble ones:

verses.pali: eko saddhammaṁ sotukāmo, eko saddhammaṁ na sotukāmo.
verses.english: one likes to hear the true teaching, one does not.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhammaṁ na sotukāmo,
verses.english: The individual who doesn’t like to hear the true teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhammaṁ sotukāmo,
verses.english: The individual who does like to hear the true teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .2
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā saddhammaṁ sotukāmā—
verses.english: Two individuals like to hear the true teaching:

verses.pali: eko ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti, eko anohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti.
verses.english: one actively listens to the teaching, one does not.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo anohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti,
verses.english: The individual who doesn’t actively listen to the teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti,
verses.english: The individual who does actively listen to the teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .3
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti—
verses.english: Two individuals actively listen to the teaching:

verses.pali: eko sutvā dhammaṁ dhāreti, eko sutvā dhammaṁ na dhāreti.
verses.english: one remembers the teaching they’ve heard, one does not.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo sutvā na dhammaṁ dhāreti,
verses.english: The individual who doesn’t remember the teaching they’ve heard

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo sutvā dhammaṁ dhāreti,
verses.english: The individual who does remember the teaching they’ve heard

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .4
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā sutvā dhammaṁ dhārenti—
verses.english: Two individuals remember the teaching they’ve heard:

verses.pali: eko dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhati, eko dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ na upaparikkhati.
verses.english: one examines the meaning of the teachings they have remembered, one does not.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ na upaparikkhati,
verses.english: The individual who does not examine the meaning of the teachings they have remembered

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhati,
verses.english: The individual who does examine the meaning of the teachings they have remembered

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .5
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhanti—
verses.english: Two individuals examine the meaning of the teachings they have remembered:

verses.pali: eko atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno, eko atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno.
verses.english: one understands the meaning and the teaching and practicesin line with the teaching, one understands the meaning and the teaching but does not practice in line with the teaching.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno,
verses.english: The individual who understands the meaning and the teaching but does not practice in line with the principle of the teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno,
verses.english: The individual who understands the meaning and the teaching and practices in line with the principle of the teaching

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .6
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Dve puggalā atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipannā—
verses.english: Two individuals understand the meaning and the teaching and practice in line with the teaching:

verses.pali: eko attahitāya paṭipanno no parahitāya, eko attahitāya ca paṭipanno parahitāya ca.
verses.english: one practices to benefit themselves but not others, and one practices to benefit both themselves and others.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno no parahitāya,
verses.english: The individual who practices to benefit themselves but not others

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
verses.english: is reprehensible in that respect.

verses.pali: Yvāyaṁ puggalo attahitāya ca paṭipanno parahitāya ca,
verses.english: The individual who practices to benefit both themselves and others

verses.pali: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso. .7
verses.english: is praiseworthy in that respect.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dvayena puggalā viditā honti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant understands individuals in terms of pairs.

verses.pali: Evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu puggalaparoparaññū hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is one who knows individuals high and low.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
verses.english: A mendicant with these seven qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ.
